events.title: The martyrdom of St. Oliver Plunkett
events.shortBlurb: The Archbishop of Armagh was hanged at Tyburn on false charges, the last Catholic martyr to die there…
body: Oliver Plunkett, Archbishop of Armagh and Primate of All Ireland, had labored quietly to rebuild the Catholic Church in Ireland under harsh penal conditions, often in hiding. Swept up in the hysteria of the fabricated “Popish Plot,” he was arrested, moved to London where a conviction could be assured, and condemned on the perjured testimony of his enemies.

On the first of July 1681 he was hanged, drawn, and quartered at Tyburn, forgiving his accusers and protesting his innocence to the end. He was the last Catholic to be martyred at Tyburn; beatified in 1920, he was canonized by Pope Paul VI in 1975.
